name: Elizabeth Warren

lean.basis: Progressive Democratic U.S. senator from Massachusetts since 2013 and 2020 presidential candidate.

current_role: U.S. senator from Massachusetts (since 2013); ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee
summary: Elizabeth Warren, a former Harvard law professor who designed the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, has been a Democratic U.S. senator from Massachusetts since 2013 and finished third in the 2020 presidential primaries. As the ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee she has led opposition to the Trump family's crypto businesses, including World Liberty Financial's bank charter, approved in August 2026.

connections.name: Barack Obama
connections.description: Obama named Warren Assistant to the President and special adviser to set up the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (2010–2011).

connections.name: World Liberty Financial
connections.description: Warren has led Senate Democratic opposition to the Trump family's crypto company: urging divestment (May 2025), pressing regulators to reject its bank charter, and introducing the Ending Presidential Corruption in Banking Act after the charter's approval in August 2026.

connections.description: A Trump critic since 2016, when she called him "a loser"; in his second term she has accused him of profiting from the presidency through crypto, saying he became "the first President in history to approve, operate, and supervise his own bank."

connections.name: Bernie Sanders
connections.description: Leading progressive allies in the Senate who have backed each other's bills, though they ran against each other in the 2020 primaries.

connections.name: Bernie Sanders
connections.description: Both sought the 2020 Democratic nomination; Warren finished third behind Biden and Sanders and withdrew on March 5, 2020.

connections.name: Joe Biden
connections.description: Warren ran against Biden in the 2020 primaries and was later one of the four finalists he considered for running mate.

connections.name: Hillary Clinton
connections.description: Warren endorsed Clinton in June 2016 and campaigned for her, including at the Democratic convention.

connections.name: Michael Bloomberg
connections.description: At a February 19, 2020 primary debate Warren attacked Bloomberg over his tax records, non-disclosure agreements and record on women and redlining.

connections.name: Jeff Sessions
connections.description: During the February 2017 debate on Sessions's attorney general nomination, Warren was formally silenced on the Senate floor for reading Coretta Scott King's letter against him.

connections.name: Chuck Schumer
connections.description: Warren has been vice chair of the Senate Democratic Caucus in Schumer's leadership since 2017.

connections.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
connections.description: Warren wrote Ocasio-Cortez's 2019 Time 100 entry and they have introduced legislation together.

connections.name: Scott Brown
connections.description: Warren unseated the Republican senator Brown in 2012.

connections.name: Jamie Raskin
connections.description: Warren campaigned with Raskin in his 2016 House race.
